passage: Air is a mixture of gases that surrounds our planet like a protective blanket. Although we cannot see it, air is present everywhere, even in the tiny spaces between soil particles and inside an empty-looking glass. Air has mass and occupies space, which is why a balloon expands when you blow into it. The atmosphere is a thin layer of air that gets thinner as we move away from the Earth's surface. Air is composed mainly of nitrogen and oxygen, with small amounts of carbon dioxide and water vapour. Water vapour is always present in the air, even on dry days, because it evaporates from oceans and lakes. Oxygen is essential for life, but it does not catch fire itself; instead, it helps other substances burn. Plants use carbon dioxide during the day to make food, but they also respire like animals, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide to stay alive. Carbon dioxide is not just a waste product; it is vital for plants to grow. Finally, aquatic animals like fish survive by using the oxygen that is already dissolved in the water, rather than breaking down water molecules themselves. Air is a dynamic mixture that supports all life on Earth through these constant processes.

items.evidence: Water vapour is always present in the air, even on dry days, because it evaporates from oceans and lakes.
items.q: Why is there water vapour in the air even on a dry, sunny day?
options: Water keeps evaporating from oceans and lakes
Dry days still bring a little rain
Only humid air can hold any water
Soil releases it only when it rains
items.explain: Water vapour comes from evaporation from oceans and lakes, so it is in the air even on dry days.

wrong.why: thinks vapour needs rain to be present
thinks vapour exists only when air is humid
mixes up soil with the source of vapour

items.evidence: Oxygen is essential for life, but it does not catch fire itself; instead, it helps other substances burn.
items.q: A candle burns in a jar of pure oxygen. What is the oxygen doing?
options: Helping the wax burn more brightly
Burning itself along with the wax
Putting out the flame slowly
Turning into the wax as it burns
items.explain: Oxygen does not burn itself; it helps other substances like wax burn.

wrong.why: thinks oxygen stops fire, like carbon dioxide
thinks a gas can turn into the fuel

items.evidence: Plants use carbon dioxide during the day to make food, but they also respire like animals, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide to stay alive.
items.q: A student says plants only take in carbon dioxide. Which fact shows this is incomplete?
options: Plants also take in oxygen to stay alive
Plants make food only during the night
Plants give out oxygen so animals breathe
Plants do not need any gas to live
items.explain: Plants respire like animals, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide to stay alive.

wrong.why: mixes up the time plants make food
thinks plants make oxygen for animals
thinks plants do not respire like animals

items.evidence: Finally, aquatic animals like fish survive by using the oxygen that is already dissolved in the water, rather than breaking down water molecules themselves.
items.q: How does a fish get the oxygen it needs to live?
options: It uses oxygen already mixed into the water
It splits water into oxygen and hydrogen
It takes oxygen out of the water molecules
It rises up and breathes only the air
items.explain: Fish use oxygen dissolved in the water; they do not break water molecules apart.

wrong.why: thinks fish break water down themselves
thinks fish use oxygen atoms of H2O
thinks fish must breathe air from above

items.evidence: The atmosphere is a thin layer of air that gets thinner as we move away from the Earth's surface.
items.q: A climber goes higher up a very tall mountain. How does the air change?
options: It becomes thinner, with less air around
It becomes thicker, with more air around
It stays the same all the way up
It becomes thinner, then goes on forever
items.explain: The atmosphere gets thinner as we move away from the Earth's surface, so higher means less air.

wrong.why: thinks air is the same at every height
thinks the atmosphere goes on forever
